source_text: ΚΑΤΗΧΗΣΙΣ ΠΡΩΤΗ. Πρὸς τοὺς μέλλοντας φωτίζεσθαι, καὶ διὰ τί λουτρὸν παλιγγενεσίας καὶ οὐκ ἀφέσεως ἁμαρτημάτων λέγεται, καὶ ὅτι ἐπικίνδυνον οὐ τὸ ἐπιορκεῖν μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ὀμνύειν, κἂν εὐορκῶμεν. αʹ. Ὡς ποθεινὸς καὶ ἐπέραστος τῶν νέων ἡμῖν ἀδελφῶν ὁ χορός· ἀδελφοὺς γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ καὶ πρὸ τῶν ὠδίνων ἤδη καλῶ, καὶ πρὸ τοῦ τόκου τὴν συγγένειαν τὴν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀσπάζομαι. Οἶδα γὰρ, οἶδα σαφῶς εἰς ὅσην μὲν ἄγεσθαι μέλλετε τιμὴν, εἰς ὅσην δὲ ἀρχήν· τοὺς δὲ ἀρχὴν μέλλοντας λαμβάνειν, καὶ πρὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς εἰώθασι τιμᾷν ἅπαντες, διὰ τῆς θεραπείας εὔνοιαν ἑαυτοῖς προαποτιθέμενοι πρὸς τὸ μέλλον. Τοῦτο δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ποιῶ νῦν· οὐ γὰρ εἰς ἀρχὴν ἄγεσθαι μέλλετε ψιλὴν, ἀλλ' εἰς βασιλείαν αὐτήν· μᾶλλον δὲ οὐκ εἰς βασιλείαν ἁπλῶς, ἀλλ' εἰς αὐτὴν τῶν οὐρανῶν τὴν βασιλείαν. Διὰ τοῦτο ὑμῶν δέομαι καὶ ἀντιβολῶ, ἵνα μνησθῆτέ μου, ὅταν ἔλθητε εἰς βασιλείαν ἐκείνην, καὶ ὅπερ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἔλεγε πρὸς τὸν ἀρχιοινοχόον· Μνήσθητί μου, ὅταν εὖ σοι γένηται· τοῦτο κἀγὼ λέγω πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄρτι· Μνήσθητέ μου ὅταν εὖ ὑμῖν γένηται. Οὐκ ἐνυπνίων ταύτην ἀπαιτῶ τὴν ἀμοιβὴν καθάπερ ἐκεῖνος· οὐ γὰρ ὀνείρατα ἦλθον διαλῦσαι ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς διηγησόμενος πράγματα, καὶ εὐαγγέλια κομίζων ἀγαθῶν τοιούτων, Οἷα οὔτε ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν, οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν, οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη· τοιαῦτά ἐστιν Ἃ ἡτοίμασεν ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν. Ὁ μὲν οὖν Ἰωσὴφ ἔλεγε πρὸς τὸν οἰνοχόον ἐκεῖνον· Ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι, καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει σε Φαραὼ εἰς τὴν ἀρχιοινοχοΐαν σου· ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ λέγω, Ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι, καὶ εἰς οἰνοχοΐαν ἐνεχθήσεσθε τυράννου· ἀλλ' ἔτι τριάκοντα ἡμέραι, καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει ὑμᾶς οὐχὶ Φαραὼ, ἀλλ' ὁ τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλεὺς εἰς τὴν ἄνω πατρίδα, εἰς τὴν ἐλευθέραν Ἱερουσαλὴμ, εἰς τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. Κἀκεῖνος μὲν ἔλεγεν, ὅτι Δώσεις τὸ ποτήριον εἰς χεῖρας τοῦ Φαραώ· ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ λέγω, ὅτι δώσετε τὸ ποτήριον εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τοῦ βασιλέως, ἀλλ' ὅτι αὐτὸς ὁ βασιλεὺς εἰς χεῖρα τὴν ὑμετέραν δώσει τὸ ποτήριον τὸ φρικτὸν καὶ πολλῆς γέμον δυνάμεως, καὶ τῆς κτίσεως τιμιώτερον ἑκατέρας. Ἴσασιν οἱ μεμυημένοι τοῦ ποτηρίου τούτου τὴν ἰσχύν· εἴσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς μικρὸν ὕστερον. Μνήσθητε οὖν, ὅταν ἔλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν ἐκείνην, ὅταν τὸ ἱμάτιον τὸ βασιλικὸν ἀπολάβητε, ὅταν τὴν πορφύραν περιβάλησθε τὴν αἵματι βαφεῖσαν Δεσποτικῷ, ὅταν διάδημα ἀναδήσησθε τῶν ἡλιακῶν ἀκτίνων φαιδροτέρας ἔχον πανταχόθεν ἐκπηδώσας λαμπηδόνας. Τοιαῦτα γὰρ τοῦ νυμφίου τὰ ἕδνα, μείζονα μὲν τῆς ἡμετέρας ἀξίας, ἄξια δὲ τῆς αὐτοῦ φιλανθρωπίας. Διὰ ταῦτα ὑμᾶς ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη καὶ πρὸ τῶν ἱερῶν ἐκείνων μακαρίζω παστάδων· οὐ μακαρίζω δὲ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπαινῶ τὴν εὐγνωμοσύνην, ὅτι μὴ καθάπερ οἱ ῥᾳθυμότεροι τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἐν ἐσχάταις ἀναπνοαῖς τῷ φωτίσματι προσήλθετε, ἀλλ' ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη καθάπερ οἰκέται εὐγνώμονες, μετὰ πολλῆς εὐνοίας ὑπακοῦσαι Δεσπότῃ παρεσκευασμένοι, τὸν αὐχένα τῆς ψυχῆς μετὰ πολλῆς ἐπιεικείας τε καὶ προθυμίας ὑπὸ τὴν ζεύγλην ἠγάγετε τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τὸν ζυγὸν ἐδέξασθε τὸν χρηστὸν, καὶ τὸ φορτίον ἐλάβετε τὸ ἐλαφρόν.
thought_title: The catechumens' future honor and the preacher's request for remembrance
orientation: John Chrysostom opens his first baptismal instruction by addressing the catechumens who are about to be baptized, celebrating their decision and asking them to remember him when they enter the kingdom of heaven.
pass_a_gloss: FIRST CATECHESIS. To those about to be baptized, and why it is called washing of regeneration and not of forgiveness of sins, and that it is dangerous not only to commit perjury, but also to swear, even if we swear truthfully. 1. How longed-for and lovely is the chorus of our new brothers; for I call you brothers already even before the birth pangs, and before the delivery I embrace the kinship with you. For I know, I know clearly into how great an honor you are about to be led, and into how great a rule; and those who are about to receive a rule, even before the rule all are accustomed to honor, storing up for themselves goodwill through service for the future. And this I myself do now; for you are about to be led not into a bare rule, but into a kingdom itself; or rather not into a kingdom simply, but into the very kingdom of the heavens. For this reason I beg you and entreat you, that you remember me, when you come into that kingdom, and what Joseph said to the chief cupbearer: Remember me, when it goes well with you; this I also say to you now: Remember me when it goes well with you. I do not demand this recompense for dreams as that man did; for I have not come to interpret dreams for you, but to tell of the things in the heavens, and bringing good tidings of such good things, Such as eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it gone up upon the heart of a human being; such are the things Which God has prepared for those who love him. Joseph then said to that cupbearer: Yet three days, and Pharaoh will restore you to your chief cupbearing; but I do not say, Yet three days, and you will be brought into the cupbearing of a tyrant; but yet thirty days, and not Pharaoh but the king of the heavens will restore you to the upper fatherland, to the free Jerusalem, to the city in the heavens. And that man said, You will give the cup into the hands of Pharaoh; but I do not say, that you will give the cup into the hands of the king, but that the king himself will give into your hand the cup that is awesome and full of much power, and more precious than either creation. Those who have been initiated know the strength of this cup; and you will know a little later. Remember then, when you come into that kingdom, when you receive back the royal garment, when you put on the purple dyed with the Master's blood, when you bind on a diadem having flashes of light leaping out from everywhere brighter than the rays of the sun. For such are the bridegroom's wedding gifts, greater than our worth, but worthy of his love for humanity. For these reasons I call you blessed from here already and before those sacred bridal chambers; and I do not only call you blessed, but I also praise your good judgment, because not like the more careless of people did you come to baptism at your last breaths, but from here already like good-minded servants, prepared with much goodwill to obey the Master, you led the neck of your soul with much gentleness and eagerness under the yoke of Christ, and you received the good yoke, and you took the light burden.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'to be baptized' for φωτίζεσθαι, avoiding the literal 'to be enlightened'.
The glossary requires this exact rendering for the baptismal term.
The title contrasts baptism as 'washing of regeneration' with mere 'forgiveness of sins'; the literal rendering preserves the contrast.
The term refers to the catechumens' sensible, well-disposed decision to prepare early rather than delay baptism; 'good judgment' captures the deliberative sense.
The adjective χρηστός is rendered 'good' to echo the Matthean language of Christ's yoke, keeping the literal sense.

pass_b_english: How lovely and desirable this company of our new brothers is! I call you brothers already, even before the birth pangs, and I embrace our kinship before the delivery. For I know—I know clearly—to what great honor you are about to be led, and to what great authority. Everyone is accustomed to honor those who are about to receive authority even before they receive it, storing up goodwill for themselves through their attentiveness for the future. This is what I am doing now. For you are about to be led not to mere authority, but to a kingdom itself—or rather, not simply to a kingdom, but to the very kingdom of heaven. Therefore I ask and beg you: remember me when you enter that kingdom. What Joseph said to the chief cupbearer—"Remember me when things go well for you" (Genesis 40:14)—this I now say to you: remember me when things go well for you. I do not ask for this reward in return for dreams, as he did. For I have not come to interpret dreams for you, but to tell you of the realities in heaven and to bring you good tidings of such blessings as "no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor has it entered the human heart—such are the things God has prepared for those who love him" (1 Corinthians 2:9). Joseph said to that cupbearer, "In three more days Pharaoh will restore you to your office of chief cupbearer" (Genesis 40:13). But I do not say, "In three more days you will be brought to the cupbearing of a tyrant." Rather, in thirty more days not Pharaoh but the King of heaven will restore you to the homeland above, to the free Jerusalem, to the city in the heavens. And Joseph said, "You will place the cup in Pharaoh's hands." But I do not say that you will place the cup in the King's hands. Rather, the King himself will place in your hand the cup that is awesome and full of great power, more precious than either of the two creations. Those who have been initiated know the strength of this cup, and you will know it a little later. Remember me, then, when you enter that kingdom, when you receive the royal robe, when you put on the purple dyed with the Master's blood, when you bind on the diadem whose radiance flashes out on every side more brightly than the rays of the sun. Such are the bridegroom's gifts—greater than our worth, but worthy of his love for humanity. For these reasons I call you blessed already now, even before those sacred bridal chambers. And I do not only call you blessed; I also praise your good judgment, because you did not come to baptism at your last breath, like the more careless among people. Instead, already now, like good and faithful servants, you have prepared yourselves to obey the Master with great goodwill. You have brought the neck of your soul under the yoke of Christ with great gentleness and eagerness, and you received the good yoke and took up the light burden.

problems.quote: more precious than either part of creation
problems.why: ἑκατέρας means 'each/every', not 'either part'; 'more precious than all creation' or 'than every creature'

edits.old: more precious than either part of creation

fixed: Changed 'either part of creation' to 'every creature' because ἑκατέρας means 'each/every', not 'either part'.

problems.why: Source says 'more precious than both' (i.e., both creation and something else), not 'every creature'.
problems.fix: more precious than either of the two creations
problems.ruling: ἑκατέρας means 'of both' (two things), not 'every creature'; 'both' refers to two items just mentioned (cup's power and awesomeness), changing meaning significantly.

edits.new: more precious than either of the two creations

fixed: The source reads 'τῆς κτίσεως τιμιώτερον ἑκατέρας', which means 'more precious than either of the two creations' (ἑκατέρας = 'of each of two'). The English 'more precious than every creature' mistranslates this, so I corrected it.

problems.source_quote: τὸν ζυγὸν ἐδέξασθε τὸν χρηστὸν, καὶ τὸ φορτίον ἐλάβετε τὸ ἐλαφρόν
problems.why: The citation is wrong: the yoke and burden language is Matthew 11:29-30, but Chrysostom quotes no verse here; the allusion is unmarked in source.
problems.fix: Remove the parenthetical citation, or note it as an allusion to Matthew 11:29-30 if editorial policy requires.
problems.ruling: Source has no scripture citation marker; translator added '(Matthew 11:30)' not in Greek text, misleading readers about source.

edits.old: and took up the light burden (Matthew 11:30).
edits.new: and took up the light burden.

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation 'Matthew 11:30' because the source does not quote a verse here; the yoke and burden language is an unmarked allusion to Matthew 11:29-30.

last_rejected.quote: more precious than either of the two creations
last_rejected.why: ἑκατέρας means 'each' not 'either of two'; 'both creations' or 'all creation' is meant.
last_rejected.fix: more precious than each part of creation
last_rejected.ruling: ἑκατέρας with κτίσεως (singular) means 'each creation' i.e. 'both creations'; 'either of the two creations' conveys same dual sense adequately.
